defect: ekf_global carried q_z = 0.02 for the vertical position state while x and y were 5e-05. 0.02 is exactly what ekf_local uses for every position axis, so it is what ekf_global started from and what was left behind when the horizontal axes were tightened. 0.02 m^2/s lets z wander 0.141 m in a second; the body is bounded by 0.05 m of suspension travel and by the ground, so it is less free than x and y.
how_it_reached_the_audit: twice, and the second way was the binding one. The inflated covariance became the padding allowance; and the loose estimate put the camera up to 76 mm off in height, which scales the projected footprint directly -- width is 2 x height x 0.7168 -- so a low estimate shrank a nominally 1.4966 m footprint to 1.408 m. Substituting the true height into the ten failing tags of the 10 km/h run made all ten pass without touching the padding.
why_it_is_not_covariance_shrinking: the filter was reporting 52.2 mm of vertical sigma against a 21.9 mm actual error: err/sigma standard deviation 0.426 where a consistent filter reads 1.0. Tightening it makes the reported uncertainty more truthful, and the actual error improved alongside it.

roll_is_not_a_process_noise_problem: roll posterior sigma 7.67 mrad already sits below the per-observation sigma of about 10.2 mrad, which motion_tilt_extra_sigma_m_s2 = 0.10 sets. Its covariance does not show the 10 Hz process-noise sawtooth z had; it rises from 1.6 to 21.9 mrad between updates that arrive at roughly 1 Hz instead of the intended 10 Hz, because 74% of the driving gravity references are rejected (1386 rejects against 488 updates). Tightening q_roll would add confidence without adding information. The rejection rate is a separate defect and the three gates are not counted separately, so it needs its own instrumentation.
